newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq eases after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq eases after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in Allied Domecq Plc slipped in pre-market trading on Tuesday after the spirits, pubs and fast food group reported in-line results but disappointed hopes of a demerger of its core businesses, traders said.
Full-year pre-tax profits fell to 575 million stg from 645 million stg in 1994/95, compared with analyst forecasts ranging from 560 to 581 million stg.
Allied shares edged lower, easing 4-1/2p to 463-1/2p.
"The results were fine. There's a bit of disappointment over the lack of demerger news after the weekend press speculation but we should see them steady up later," said a trader.

Allied chairman Sir Christopher Hogg said the board had thoroughly reviewed the demerger issue and was quite clear that the best way to improve shareholder value was to improve operating performance and that this should be the overriding objective for the foreseeable future.
He said the board was intent on developing the group's two principal businesses - the Spirits & Wine and Retailing businesses - to be leaders in their respective industries.
"The figures were very much in line with expectations. Some people had been worried the dividend may be cut but it has been maintained and that's a positive," said one analyst.
"The theme going forward is very much focussing on core businesses but overall it's much as anticipated."
The company said the corporate restructuring programme had been largely completed by the sale of Carlsberg-Tetley and food companies.

U.S. spirits de-stocking was the main factor in a 14 percent fall in Spirits & Wine trading profits while retailing profits rose 4 percent led by accelerated growth in pub brands. "The company has said they can grow earnings and that's the way to create shareholder value and they've got to show they can do it," said another analyst.

"There's still a lot of scepticism that they have to dispose of. There are no surprises in the numbers and the divisions have gone in the direction expected but if you were somone who wanted action -- a demerger or management change -- you haven't got either and there will be disappointment."

Allied said that the board was determined that the group should deliver shareholder value up to the best standards of the industries in which it is engaged and the management's overriding priority was the creation of this by improved financial performance.

The Spirits & Wine division would benefit from the increasing focus on key brand/market combinations, more favourable shipment patterns and from efficiency gains, it said, while the sale of Carlsberg-Tetley would facilitate the development of the pub business.
